title: 我叫布小谷  (My Name Is Bu Xiaogu)

segments.t: Welcome to Behind the Scenes. We begin backstage on finale night of the hit singing show Twelve Singers, before top media student Bu Xiaogu introduces herself and compares entering the workplace to jumping into a boiling hotpot. Listen to the scene first.
这是谁的呀？
你到位没有？
布小谷到位！
观众朋友们，欢迎各位！
今天是十二歌王决赛之夜！
我叫布小谷。
我是传媒学院的研究生，年级第一名。
职场是一个火锅，想想真的够吓人的。
该下锅时还是得下！
Now let's walk through each line. Backstage is loud and hurried, so a crew member checks an unclaimed prop.
这是谁的呀？
'Whose is this?' Notice how "shei de" adds "de" right after "shei", 'who', to turn it into 'whose'. Soft final "ya" keeps a quick backstage check from sounding barked.
你到位没有？
'Are you in position yet?' Putting "meiyou" at the very end of a statement is an everyday way to ask 'yet?'. Inside it, "dao wei" literally means reach your spot.
布小谷到位！
'Bu Xiaogu is in position!' Xiaogu calls out her full name instead of "wo", 'I', so the stage manager knows right away which person on the headset is ready.
观众朋友们，欢迎各位！
'Friends in the audience, welcome everyone!' Chinese stage hosts warmly add "pengyoumen", 'friends', after "guanzhong", 'audience', and follow with polite "gewei" for 'everyone here'.
今天是十二歌王决赛之夜！

'Tonight is the finals night of Twelve Singers!' Even when English says 'tonight' here, "jintian" is the everyday word for 'today', while "zhi ye" links 'finals' to 'night' in a grand broadcast title.
我叫布小谷。
'My name is Bu Xiaogu.' Remember "wo jiao" whenever you introduce yourself: "jiao" means 'be called', and your full name follows straight after with surname "Bu" first.
我是传媒学院的研究生，年级第一名。

'I am a graduate student at the Media College, first in my year.' Mandarin builds affiliation from bigger to smaller, so "chuanmei xueyuan", 'Media College', comes before "yanjiusheng", 'graduate student'.
职场是一个火锅，想想真的够吓人的。
'The workplace is a hotpot; just thinking about it is scary enough.' Repeating the action word as "xiangxiang" means 'think about it a bit', and "xiaren" literally says 'scare people'.
该下锅时还是得下！

'When it is time to jump into the pot, you still have to jump in!' Two obligation words team up here: "gai" means 'should' when the moment arrives, and "dei" means 'have to'. Now listen to the whole opening scene again from start to finish.
这是谁的呀？
你到位没有？
布小谷到位！
观众朋友们，欢迎各位！
今天是十二歌王决赛之夜！
我叫布小谷。
我是传媒学院的研究生，年级第一名。
职场是一个火锅，想想真的够吓人的。
该下锅时还是得下！

That brings us back to campus, just before Xiaogu makes the biggest career choice of her student life. You heard how to introduce yourself, check whether someone is ready, and welcome a crowd. Until next time!
下次见！
